thresholds.note: The 54.6 ug/m3 PM2.5 value is an hourly peak inside the 24 h window; comparing it with a 24 h AQO or WHO guideline is a screening comparison, not a legal compliance determination.

anomaly_assessment.rule: false when (matched_hour_z < 2.0 or event NO2 peak <= the preceding 14-day matched-hour maximum) and the other-17-station mean NO2 rise is >= 10 ug/m3; true only when z >= 2.0, the event peak exceeds the preceding maximum, the network mean rise is < 5 ug/m3, and the nearest-station PM2.5 excess is >= 5 ug/m3; otherwise indeterminate
anomaly_assessment.caveat: The peak-to-mean ratio is a screening signal, not causal attribution. The matched-hour z-score, the territory-wide network contrast and the near-calm wind do not support a single-source plume.

notes: Read-only database reference; no LLM and no database writes.
The peak-to-mean ratio is a screening signal, not causal attribution. The matched-hour z-score, the territory-wide network contrast and the near-calm wind do not support a single-source plume.
Matched-hour baseline: Tai Po NO2 at 20:00 on 2025-11-26 against the same clock hour on the 14 preceding days (2025-11-12 to 2025-11-25), using the sample standard deviation (ddof=1).
Network contrast: each station's mean over the event evening (2025-11-26 18:00-23:00) minus its mean over the same clock-hours on the 14 preceding days; the network mean uses the other 17 stations.
OSM building counts are proximity-screening counts from the ingested 2026 snapshot, not the paper's 1,090 total / 293 residential numbers.
The fire-site-centred school count is 45; the station-centred check_agent truth is 53. Both are recorded so the difference is explicit.
The wind value is near-calm (0.389 m/s from 207 degrees/SW), consistent with the Tolo basin narrative rather than a strong ventilation case.
